# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73 (Bu-Vb Pc73)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc73
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73
**Title (English, from literature):** Deception
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73, known as *Mohana* ("Deception"), concerns a monk who feigns ignorance during the recitation of the monastic code, deceptively claiming that he did not know a rule was included in the Pātimokkha; committing this offense requires confession and expiation (*pācittiya*). The word commentary (*padabhājaniya* or "Old Commentary") preserved within the Vibhaṅga explains technical legal phrases such as *anāropite* and *āropite*, describing whether a formal charge has or has not been brought against the monk [Horner 1966]. Sukumar Dutt observes that the text's injunction—that "the offence arising therefrom is to be dealt with according to the proper form" (*yañca tattha āpattiṁ āpanno tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo*)—presupposes formal legal procedures not explicitly detailed in the Pātimokkha itself, appearing to contemplate an act of censure (*tajjaniya-kamma*) for foolishness or dissimulation [Dutt 1924].

The rule corresponds to rule 73 of the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and is treated in the *Parivāra*, with a counterpart in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 151). Comprehensive parallels exist across all major Vinaya lineages—including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions—preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan translations.
